label: Flying fragments: discs, struck tools, split rims
summary: Grinding wheels and cut-off discs can burst at full speed, chisels and punches with mushroomed heads shed sharp steel when struck, and multi-piece truck rims can blow apart while a tyre is inflated, throwing parts at up to 210 km/h (130 mph). They can cause serious injury or death. Snapping straps, chains and cables are covered under Lines under load.
signs: Grinding wheels and cut-off discs that are chipped, cracked, warped, dropped, or past the expiry date stamped on them (usually 3 years from manufacture)
A wheel or disc marked for a lower speed than the grinder's rpm, or a grinder with its guard removed
A wobble, vibration or odd noise when a wheel spins up
Chisels, punches, wedges and drift pins with mushroomed, cracked or chipped heads, and hammers or axes with loose or cracked handles
Multi-piece (split) rims with a separate side ring or lock ring, on trucks, trailers, tractors and cranes; a split rim can be mounted inside a one-piece wheel
Tyres that have been run flat or badly underinflated, and rim parts that are cracked, bent, corroded or mismatched
do: Before fitting a wheel or disc, check its marked maximum speed is at least the grinder's rpm, and keep the guard on
Ring-test wheels larger than 10 cm (4 in): tap gently with a non-metal tool; a dull or cracked sound means scrap it

Stand aside, out of the wheel's plane, at every start-up. Run a newly fitted wheel at full speed for a minute before grinding with nobody in line with the guard opening; on a hand-held grinder, point the opening under a bench or into a steel drum
On a bench grinder, set the tool rest within 3 mm (1/8 in) of the wheel, never while the wheel is moving, and keep a tongue or movable guard at 6 mm (1/4 in) wheel exposure
Use light, steady pressure; don't force, twist or bend a cutting disc
Keep chisels, punches and wedges free of mushroomed heads: dress them or retire them

Split rims: deflate completely by removing the valve core before loosening wheel nuts or touching a ring. Inflate only inside a cage or restraint, with a clip-on chuck and a long hose so you stand out of the path
dont: Don't grind on the side of a regular wheel, or clamp a hand grinder in a vice
Don't use a chisel as a screwdriver: the tip can snap off and fly
Don't strike rim parts with a steel or hard-faced hammer, hammer rings while the tyre holds air, or reinflate a tyre that was run flat or underinflated
Don't weld, braze or heat cracked, bent or damaged rim parts
Don't stand in line with a wheel spinning up or a rim being inflated
ppe: Safety glasses every time, with a face shield over them for grinding and cutting
Safety boots and hearing protection for grinding and tyre work
Keep bystanders away, or in the same eye and face protection
firstAid: Speck in the eye: don't rub or press on it; blink, then flush gently with running water. If it won't come out, or something is stuck in the eye, steady it without pressing and get medical help
Leave fragments embedded in the body in place; pad round them without pressing and bandage the pads in place

Heavy bleeding: firm direct pressure and a dressing. If that fails on a limb, a tourniquet 5–10 cm (2–4 in) above the wound and at least 2.5 cm (1 in) above any joint, tightened until bleeding stops, time noted
Struck by a rim part or wheel piece: keep them still; after a head blow watch for confusion, drowsiness or vomiting, and watch everyone hit for shock: cool clammy skin, fast breathing, thirst
